title: Molecular Insights into the Interaction Between Metformin and Caffeine: The Time-Dependent Antagonism and Modulation of p53 Signaling in Cancer Cells.
authors: Zeljkovic, Vesna; Bogavac, Mirjana; Dekic, Milan; Minic, Slavisa; Mahmutovic, Elvis; Kunkin, Vanja; Markovic, Zoran; Karaman, Maja
one_liner_zh: 该文研究二甲双胍与咖啡因在癌细胞中的联合抗肿瘤效应及p53信号调控，属纯细胞实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Background: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, with treatment efficacy often limited by drug resistance and adverse effects. Drug repurposing offers promising opportunities for developing novel anticancer strategies. This study evaluated the cytotoxic, antiproliferative, and pro-apoptotic effects of metformin and caffeine, administered individually and in combination, in human cancer cell lines, as well as their potential interaction mechanisms. Methods: Human cervical carcinoma (HeLa), lung adenocarcinoma (A549), and colorectal carcinoma (HT29) cell lines were treated with metformin (0.05-50 mM) and caffeine (0.5-5 mM), either alone or in combination, for 24 and 48 h. Cell viability and proliferation were assessed using Trypan Blue and sulforhodamine B (SRB) assays. Apoptosis was analyzed by Annexin V/propidium iodide flow cytometry, and p53 expression in HeLa cells was determined by ELISA. Statistical analysis was performed using a one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test. Results: Metformin induced dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity in all tested cell lines, with the lowest IC(50) values observed in HeLa and A549 cells after 48 h (2.28 and 3.30 mM, respectively; p < 0.05). Caffeine showed moderate antiproliferative activity, with the strongest effects observed at 2.03 mM in HeLa cells and 2.01 mM in HT29 cells (p < 0.05). The combined treatment produced effects that varied depending on both the cell line and exposure time. At earlier time points, transient synergistic effects were observed in certain cell lines, particularly HeLa cells; however, these effects were not sustained over time. With prolonged exposure, the interaction shifted predominantly toward antagonistic effects, indicating the reduced overall efficacy of the combination compared with the expected additive outcomes. Increased apoptosis and elevated p53 expression further supported the activation of tumor-suppressive pathways. Conclusions: Metformin exhibited significant anticancer activity in vitro, supporting its potential repurposing in oncology. However, the addition of caffeine did not uniformly enhance its efficacy and appeared to exert context-dependent effects. Further in vivo studies are required to confirm the clinical relevance of these findings.
abstract_zh: 背景：癌症仍是全球重大健康挑战，治疗效果常受限于耐药性和不良反应。药物再利用为开发新型抗癌策略提供了有前景的机会。本研究评估了二甲双胍和咖啡因单独及联合给药在人癌细胞系中的细胞毒性、抗增殖和促凋亡作用，以及其潜在相互作用机制。方法：人宫颈癌（HeLa）、肺腺癌（A549）和结直肠癌（HT29）细胞系分别用二甲双胍（0.05-50 mM）和咖啡因（0.5-5 mM）单独或联合处理24和48小时。使用台盼蓝和磺基罗丹明B（SRB）实验评估细胞活力和增殖。通过Annexin V/碘化丙啶流式细胞术分析凋亡，并用ELISA测定HeLa细胞中p53表达。统计分析采用单因素方差分析后进行Tukey事后检验。结果：二甲双胍在所有测试细胞系中诱导剂量和时间依赖性细胞毒性，48小时后在HeLa和A549细胞中观察到最低IC(50)值（分别为2.28和3.30 mM；p < 0.05）。咖啡因显示出中等抗增殖活性，在HeLa细胞中2.03 mM和HT29细胞中2.01 mM时观察到最强效果（p < 0.05）。联合治疗产生的效果因细胞系和暴露时间而异。在较早时间点，某些细胞系（尤其是HeLa细胞）中观察到短暂的协同效应；然而，这些效应随时间未能持续。随着暴露时间延长，相互作用主要转向拮抗效应，表明联合治疗的整体疗效低于预期加性结果。凋亡增加和p53表达升高进一步支持肿瘤抑制通路的激活。结论：二甲双胍在体外表现出显著的抗癌活性，支持其在肿瘤学中再利用的潜力。然而，咖啡因的添加并未统一增强其疗效，且似乎产生情境依赖性效应。需要进一步的体内研究来确认这些发现的临床相关性。
